summary:
JEEVA is a proposed contactless astronaut health-monitoring platform designed to monitor health during space missions without requiring additional wearable sensors. It combines two technologies: camera-based monitoring using Remote Photoplethysmography (rPPG) and Computer Vision to estimate heart rate and identify facial and behavioural changes, and voice analysis using Speech Signal Processing (SSP) to track vocal biomarkers and changes in speech patterns.

JEEVA also incorporates a personal health digital twin, which establishes an astronaut's baseline using pre-flight health data and compares it with measurements collected throughout the mission. This helps identify potentially concerning changes for further assessment. Future development will include cognitive assessments, such as reaction-time and alertness tests. By exploring accessible, laptop-based health monitoring, JEEVA aims to make health assessment more flexible and accessible in challenging environments.
details:
JEEVA is a contactless astronaut health-monitoring platform designed to address the challenges of monitoring crew health during space missions, where access to immediate medical assistance is limited and traditional wearable monitoring can be restrictive.

JEEVA integrates camera-based monitoring using Remote Photoplethysmography (rPPG) and computer vision to estimate heart rate, alongside voice analysis using Speech Signal Processing (SSP) to examine vocal characteristics such as pitch, speech rate, pauses and changes associated with fatigue or stress. These measurements are brought together through an integrated health dashboard. A personal digital twin establishes an astronaut's individual health baseline using pre-flight data and compares it with measurements collected throughout the mission. The prototype also demonstrates Psychomotor Vigilance Testing (PVT) to assess reaction time and alertness.

The project's main innovation is combining multiple contactless monitoring methods with personalized health tracking in one accessible platform. Rather than relying solely on universal health thresholds, JEEVA considers changes relative to each astronaut's individual baseline. This could help identify potentially concerning changes earlier and support further medical assessment.

We developed a browser-based interactive prototype, hosted on Netlify, designed to use a standard laptop, webcam and microphone without additional wearable sensors. Our team considered accessibility, privacy, data security, signal quality, lighting, movement, microphone conditions, microgravity and measurement reliability. The system provides estimates rather than medical diagnoses, and further testing and clinical validation would be required before operational use.

Future development will expand cognitive assessments, alertness monitoring and health-data integration. Our vision is to transform contactless health monitoring into a practical, personalized solution that can support people both in space and on Earth.
